description: Flutter plugin for age verification and age gating, wrapping the Google Play Age Signals API on Android and Apple's DeclaredAgeRange API on iOS 26+.
rules: This plugin reports age signals the OS already holds. It is not identity verification, document scanning, or KYC, and it never returns a date of birth. Only an age range and an assurance tier are available.
Access the plugin through the singleton `AgeRangeSignals.instance`. There is no public constructor.

Import only `package:age_range_signals/age_range_signals.dart`. The `age_range_signals_method_channel` and `age_range_signals_platform_interface` libraries are federated-plugin plumbing, not application API.

Since 0.8.0 the flow is two calls: `await requestAgeSignalsAccess()` first, then `checkAgeSignals()` only when it returns `AgeSignalsAccessStatus.shared`. Calling `checkAgeSignals()` alone skips the access grant.

Call `initialize()` on both platforms. iOS requires `ageGates` and throws `NotInitializedException` without them. Play ignores gates, but Android uses your highest gate as the bar for `verified` (falling back to 18), so skipping it changes the verdict.
On iOS, Apple accepts 1 to 3 age gates and requires at least 2 years between consecutive gates, so `[13, 16, 18]` is valid and `[13, 14]` is rejected by the OS.

`status` is the verdict, `ageRangeSource` is the assurance. `verified` means the reported band starts at or above your highest gate; `supervised` means it falls below. Both platforms apply the same rule, so one check means the same thing on each.
A tier is never proof of age. `AgeRangeSource.tierD` means an ID was checked, and that ID can read 12. Use `ageRangeSource` only to apply a minimum assurance policy, never as the verdict.

`AgeSignalsStatus` values to handle: verified, unknown, declined, supervised, supervisedApprovalPending, supervisedApprovalDenied. `declared` is deprecated and never returned; read `ageRangeSource == AgeRangeSource.tierA` instead.

Status platform split: the two supervisedApproval values are Android only, `declined` is iOS only. On Android a refusal surfaces as `AgeSignalsAccessStatus.notShared` from the access call, not as `declined`.

`requestAgeSignalsAccess()` returns `AgeSignalsAccessStatus`: shared, notShared (a decline, not an error), verificationRequired (send the user to the Play Store; no in-app flow), unknown. iOS always returns shared.

`AgeRangeSource` (Android), weakest to strongest: tierA self-declared, tierB parent- or guardian-managed, tierC assessed via credit card, email, selfie, government ID or tax ID, tierD government ID plus selfie or a digital ID.

`SignificantChangeStatus` (Android, supervised users) is approved, pending or declined. Pending or declined reports supervisedApprovalPending/Denied whatever the age, because an outstanding guardian decision is actionable either way.
`ageLower`/`ageUpper` are null when nothing was shared. A `verified` result always has `ageLower` set, since that is how the verdict is derived, and `ageUpper` is null for the open-ended top band.
Android is ActivityAware because Play hosts a sharing prompt. Without an attached Activity, `requestAgeSignalsAccess()` throws `ApiErrorException` with code `PRESENTATION_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE`.

`useMockData: true` throws `MockDataNotAllowedException` in non-debuggable Android builds. The fake manager forges age signals, so never suggest enabling it in release; build a debuggable variant instead.
`useMockData` and `mockData` are Android only, backed by Google's `FakeAgeSignalsManager`. They are silently ignored on iOS, which has no testing utility and requires a real device on iOS 26.2+.
Catch `AgeSignalsException` as the base type for all plugin errors. Each carries a `code` and a `details` string holding platform-specific diagnostics.

Exception subclasses, all suffixed `Exception`: ApiNotAvailable, UnsupportedPlatform, NotInitialized, MissingEntitlement, ApiError, PlayServices, NetworkError, UserNotSignedIn, UserCancelled, MockDataNotAllowed.

`getRequiredRegulatoryFeatures()` needs iOS 26.4+ and an Xcode 26.4+ build. It returns an empty set on Android and throws `UnsupportedPlatformException` on older iOS, so an empty set always means no regulatory action is required, never unknown.

`showSignificantUpdateAcknowledgment()` throws `UnsupportedPlatformException` on Android and iOS below 26.4. Apple reports user dismissal with the same error as real unavailability, so `ApiNotAvailableException` is not proof the sheet never showed.

Platform floors: Android API 23+ with Google Play services; iOS 26.0 for the base API, 26.2 for regional eligibility, 26.4 for regulatory features. iOS also requires Apple's DeclaredAgeRange entitlement.

`AgeSignalsResult.significantChangeApprovalDate` was named `mostRecentApprovalDate` before 0.8.0. The old name still works as a deprecated alias on the result, the mock data, both constructors and `copyWith`.

Google Play policy allows Age Signals data only for delivering age-appropriate experiences. Never route it to advertising, marketing, profiling, or analytics. That risks API termination and app suspension, so never log the result to an analytics SDK.
